subject: Post-call: Halcyon Health — inference fit & integration next steps
messages:
From: Samantha Ortiz <samantha@halcyonhealth.com>
To: kimberly.park@redwood.ai, mateo.alvarez@redwood.ai
Date: Tue, 15 Sep 2026 14:03:00 -0700
Subject: Intro + call recap: Redwood fit for Halcyon inferencing

Kimberly / Mateo — thanks again for the demo and discussion earlier today. Quick recap from our side and a few clarifying questions so we can align internally: 

1) Primary pain points we described:
- Current triage assistant has 700ms+ median latency for short prompts; spikes to 1.8s under load.
- Our current vector search + reranker misses critical entity matching in clinical notes (lots of false positives).
- Cost per 1M tokens is a concern given volume (expecting ~150M tokens/month at pilot scale).

2) Goals for a pilot
- 100ms median for sub-256-token prompts for conversational triage.
- Demonstrable lift in retrieval precision using embeddings + rerank (we have labeled eval set).
- Structured outputs for clinical fields (JSON schema) to avoid heavy post-processing.
- Maintain HIPAA-compliant controls and clear audit log for inference.

3) Immediate asks from our procurement/infra teams:
- Ballpark pricing for a 2-week pilot (throughput target: 50 rps sustained, 200 rps burst).
- SDK changes required for streaming + function-calling support, and estimated eng effort.
- Sample latency percentiles on similar workloads / model variants you recommend.
- SOC2 report and any HIPAA attestation info.

I attached our requirements workbook (halcyon-requirements.xlsx) to this message — hopefully that helps with sizing.

Next step from us: procurement wants a short written summary and an integration scope to share with the infra team. Can you send a one-page pilot plan and any engineering notes?

Samantha
Samantha Ortiz
Head of Platform Integrations 
Halcyon Health

Subject: Re: Intro + call recap: Redwood fit for Halcyon inferencing

Samantha — great to meet you and thanks for the workbook. Appreciate the clear goals; below is our actionable recap + proposed pilot scope.

TL;DR: We can run an embed+rerank pilot with streaming/function-call SDK support and structured-output mapping. Pilot target: 2 weeks, validate latency and precision improvement on your eval set.

Confirmed pain points (we heard):
- Latency: aim for sub-100ms median on short prompts; p95 target under 300ms for pilot traffic profile.
- Retrieval quality: experiment with dense embeddings + a lightweight neural reranker; use labeled set for evaluation.
- Structured outputs: map model responses to your clinical JSON schema via function calling + output validators.
- Compliance: pilot runs on a private tenant with audit logs; SOC2 link below for docs.

Proposed pilot deliverables (what Redwood will provide):
- Pilot plan (attached): redwood-integration-proposal.pdf — includes scope, timelines, and success criteria.
- SDK adjustments: streaming + function-calling hooks, example validators for structured outputs.
- Performance targets: provide latency matrix for recommended model configs (quantized 8-bit variant + CPU fallback) after we run a small synthetic workload against your sample set.
- Ops: logging, prefix/KV caching enabled for the pilot; rollback policy and model fallback included.

Owner / contacts:
- Engagement lead: Kimberly Park (me) — commercial / rollout coordination.
- Technical lead: Mateo Alvarez (copied) — will own integration path, SDK changes, and perf validation.
- Solutions engineering: Ben Carter (copied) — will help tune reranker and eval metrics.

Next steps / asks from Halcyon:
1) Confirm pilot dates (we recommended Oct 5–19 but can shift).
2) Share a sample of your eval set (anonymized) and expected traffic shape (50 rps sustained target).
3) Procurement: contact for SOC2/Security packet and to start an SOW if pilot approved.

I've attached our one-page proposal. Mateo — tagging you for the technical follow-up and a brief estimate on SDK work.

Thanks,

From: mateo.alvarez@redwood.ai (Mateo Alvarez)
To: samantha@halcyonhealth.com, kimberly.park@redwood.ai
Cc: ben.carter@redwood.ai
Date: Wed, 16 Sep 2026 08:46:00 -07:00
Subject: Technical notes — embedding/rerank approach + SDK changes

Samantha / Kimberly — following up with the technical sketch and a small set of attachments (sample-api-log.txt) from our internal micro-benchmarks. High level notes: 

1) Embedding + rerank approach
- Use 1536-d embeddings (dense) for initial nearest-neighbor recall.
- Train a small cross-encoder reranker on your labeled pairs (we can provide the recipe). Expected improvement: +6–12% precision@10 on similar clinical datasets.

2) Latency profile & model choices
- For short prompts (<256 tokens) we expect median latency ~70–110ms with continuous batching + KV cache on A100/80GB equiv. Quantized 8-bit runs at ~90–130ms; p95 depends on burst profile but should remain <350ms with our autoscaler config.

3) SDK changes (estimate)
- Streaming: add a streaming iterator on the client (two small endpoints). Effort: ~3 dev-days to add wrappers + tests.
- Function calling / structured outputs: provide a small SDK helper to validate/deserialize JSON schema and rehydrate missing fields. Effort: ~2 dev-days.
- Integration hooks for reranker: example pipeline and evaluation harness. Effort: ~3–4 dev-days for the pilot artifacts.

Net engineering effort for a pilot-ready integration: ~1 engineer x 2 weeks (includes tests, example notebooks, and perf runs). We will prioritize the streaming path and function-calling support first.

Attachments included: sample-api-log.txt (synthetic p50/p95 numbers), and a short snippet showing the SDK call pattern for streaming + funcall.

If you can share a small anonymized batch (500–1,000 records) we can run a focused perf pass and return a latency/p95 matrix by end of next week.

—Mateo
Mateo Alvarez
Principal Engineer, Serving Runtime
Redwood Inference
